protocol: 10 rounds x 16 passes over the complete selected subset; one full-pass warmup; implementation order shuffled with fixed seed; upper median batch
invariants: ordered IDs, hits, distances, expansions and adjacency equal before/memo/after for every query; counted/normal IDs equal; every timed pass equals audited checksum; zero unqualified distances
nodeann: independent native hnswlib copy; fixed local n=k; no n sweep in this diagnosis; recall=1; comparison is not exact-equal-recall
representation: unchanged item graph, vectors, entries and owner mapping; single frontier; no local-graph fallback or per-query copied graph
width_note: fixed requested ef32/ef128; unchanged legacy merged caller min(ef,eligible), then max(k,ef) inside executor; NodeANN uses requested ef per local graph
reuse: run2 uses the identical binaries from run1; per-implementation shared workspace, never per-query full-sized visited arrays
limitations: two runs do not establish confidence intervals
one recursive k100 many-owner subset had a 1.3% slowdown in run1, not in run2
binary_hash_note: Binary SHA256 captured after both runs; repeated runs were invoked without rebuilding, not independently hash-attested at each process start.
